newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dell aims to outgrow Japan PC market by 2-3 times.
newsitem.headline: Dell aims to outgrow Japan PC market by 2-3 times.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp is looking to increase sales in Japan at two to three times the growth rate in the overall market, chairman Michael Dell said on Tuesday.
"If the market is growing by 20 percent, we would like to grow by 40 to 60 percent," the visiting chairman told Reuters after an executive luncheon at a Tokyo hotel.

He also said that the company, one of the world's largest PC makers, will boost its staff in Japan by twofold or threefold in the next three to four years. The company currently employs about 250 staff at its Japanese unit.
Dell Computer sold 133,000 PCs in 1996 in Japan, accounting for two percent of the market, according to the research firm IDC Japan Ltd.
NEC Corp, Japan's top PC maker, shipped 2.6 million units, taking 33 percent of the domestic market, IDC Japan said.
In a move to boost sales in Japan, Dell on Tuesday started an on-line commerce service on the Internet for Japanese customers.
Dell started the Internet shopping service in the United States in last July where sales have exceeded $1 million per day, the company says.
Dell said that there is a transition in buying patterns among PC users in which more users are buying directly from a manufacturer rather than a retailer.
A spokesman said Dell expects half of the company's total sales eventually will come from the Internet.
The company has also launched a separate desk-top personal computer brand in Japan.
The Dimension XPS series use Intel Corp's MMX Pentium processors, and is targeted at small and medium-sized firms and individuals.
A low-end model in the new series is priced at 218,900 yen ($1,772,) and a high-end model at 347,900 yen ($2,821).
The company has been marketing its OptiPlex brand to business users since it begun its operation in Japan in 1993. ($1=123 yen)
